study type: descriptive, prospective, longitudinal quality improvement project
exposure: Web-based educational training on hand hygiene
outcome: behavioral and attitudinal factors related to hand hygiene
cohort: Clinical staff in the women's care center (Labor and Delivery, Mother and Baby, and Obstetrics Emergency Room) at a large, urban, tertiary care hospital in the Midwestern United States.
finding: Although the web-based hand hygiene training did not significantly improve knowledge or attitudes, it was associated with a statistically significant reduction in post-Cesarean surgical site infections.
mod_finding: A web-based hand hygiene intervention was associated with a significant reduction in surgical site infections following Cesarean sections.
